_meta.indication: Durezol (difluprednate ophthalmic emulsion) 0.05%, a topical corticosteroid, is indicated for the treatment of inflammation and pain associated with ocular surgery.

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, double-masked, randomized, vehicle (placebo)-controlled trial; patients dosed either BID or QID for 14 days
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with an anterior chamber cell grade ≥ 2 (cell count of 10 or higher) after cataract surgery
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of ITT subjects with complete clearing (count = 0) of anterior chamber cells by Day 8
pivotal_trials.n: QID n=55, placebo n=105 (FDA primary endpoint arms)
pivotal_trials.result: QID: clearing (=0) of AC cells by Day 8 in 13/55 (23.6%) vs placebo 11/105 (10.5%); difference 13.2% (95% CI -0.9, 27.2); p=0.0302

pivotal_trials.design: Phase 3, double-masked, randomized, vehicle (placebo)-controlled trial of identical design to 002A; patients dosed BID or QID for 14 days
pivotal_trials.population: Subjects with an anterior chamber cell grade ≥ 2 (cell count of 10 or higher) after cataract surgery
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proportion of ITT subjects with complete clearing (count = 0) of anterior chamber cells by Day 8
pivotal_trials.n: QID n=52, placebo n=113 (FDA primary endpoint arms)
pivotal_trials.result: QID: clearing (=0) of AC cells by Day 8 in 11/52 (21.2%) vs placebo 6/113 (5.3%); difference 15.8% (95% CI 2.6, 29.1); p=0.0012

key_safety: Ocular adverse reactions in 5–15% of subjects included corneal edema, ciliary and conjunctival hyperemia, eye pain, photophobia, posterior capsule opacification, anterior chamber cells, anterior chamber flare, conjunctival edema, and blepharitis; reactions in 1–5% included reduced visual acuity, punctate keratitis, eye inflammation, and iritis. Class steroid risks include elevated intraocular pressure, cataract formation, secondary ocular infection, and delayed healing.
target_moa: Difluprednate is a synthetic glucocorticoid receptor agonist (a difluorinated derivative of prednisolone); corticosteroids inhibit the inflammatory response, suppressing release of arachidonic acid and inflammatory mediators such as prostaglandins and leukotrienes.

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was held on May 29, 2008; the committee concurred with the potential approval of the application and raised no new issues of safety or efficacy.

description.text: Updated Pediatric Use labeling for treatment of inflammation following cataract surgery in children 0 to 3 years of age

citations.quote: This "Prior Approval" supplemental new drug application provides for revisions to the Pediatric Use section of the package insert to reflect the results from Clinical Study C-10-004 entitled, "A Phase 3B, Multicenter, Randomized, Double-Masked, Parallel-Group, Active-Controlled Study of the Safety and Efficacy of Difluprednate Ophthalmic Emulsion, 0.05% (Durezol) 4 Times Daily (QID) and Prednisolone Acetate Ophthalmic Suspension, 1.0% (Pred Forte) QID for the Treatment of Inflammation Following Cataract Surgery in Children 0 to 3 Years of Age."

summary.text: Durezol (difluprednate), a new molecular entity topical ophthalmic corticosteroid, was reviewed as a 505(b) NDA and approved June 23, 2008 for inflammation and pain associated with ocular surgery, based on two Phase 3 double-masked, randomized, vehicle-controlled trials; an advisory committee concurred with approval and no special designations were applied.

citations.quote: Durezol (ST-601) is a topical formulation of difluprednate (new molecular entity) that is an ophthalmic corticosteroid emulsion for topical ocular instillation.

Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated December 21, 2007, received December 26, 2007, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act for Durezol (difluprednate ophthalmic emulsion) 0.05%.
Two phase 3, double-masked, randomized, vehicle-controlled clinical trials evaluating ST-601 in the treatment of inflammation and pain following cataract surgery.
